title: A year with Fletcher Henderson: Hawkins, Bobby Stark, and the arrangements
summary: In the Henderson band he was most moved by Bobby Stark, heard Hawkins and Benny Carter battle, and thought the arrangements terrific.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, how long were you with Fletcher?
I think I was with Fletcher, I imagine almost a year.
Well, Cootie, you don't say anything about that band. What about those mammoth talents in that band?
Oh, we had some talent in that band.
I mean, what did you feel when you first heard of Hawk? Didn't that impress you?
I was more impressed with Bobby Stark than I was with Hawk.
Yeah. Because Bobby Stark was a trumpet player.
I see. You mean you really had no ears
That is a funny thing. I mean, what about Benny Carter? He had some ideas.
Well, I'll tell you. Well, I told you, Bobby Stark was the only one that moved me. And Greene.
So a little later on, I used to listen to Hawk and Benny Carter battle each other. Sometimes used to have jam sessions right on the bandstand.
So that didn't bother me, not at all, you know.
What about -- well, there was Buster.
Oh. Well, what about that rhythm section? That was Clarence Holiday, wasn't it?
And who was the bass player? Kirby?
Escudero was there for a little while.
Well, I remember you being awful fussy about rhythm sections in Duke's band. Weren't you fussy about it in other people's bands?
Why? You just don't care what they give behind you.
I wasn't fussy then. About it. You know.
Because you felt you didn't need it, you mean. You --
No, I wasn't looking for it. I wasn't looking for it then.
No kidding. Well, didn't those arrangements please you?
Oh, yeah, yeah. He had some terrific arrangements.
Yeah. Like some of those queer motions and some of those things, and those strange keys.
Yeah. Yeah, the arrangements was terrific. And he played in all hard keys, funny keys, everything. Sharps and flats. Five flats, five sharps, six sharps, everything.
And nobody in that band minded that?
Yeah. Oh, yeah. He had all terrific musicians.
Did you like Fletcher's own arrangements?
Yeah. I didn't know which ones was Fletcher's and who else.

No kidding. Well, you did later, when Fletcher's arrangements gave that sound to the Goodman band. They did, didn't they? You remember, when the Goodman band was just coming into its prime, that was what it sounded like. It was Fletcher's arrangements. "Stealing Apples", "Sometimes I'm Happy" --
-- and those things, you know. It got a sound that really came out of Fletcher. I don't mean that it sounded like Fletcher's band, but that it was something that was related to Fletcher, wasn't it?
Yeah. That's the only band, actually, that really moved me. Was the Goodman band.
